---
title: "Welcome"
---

Welcome to **R for Health Research** — an introduction to R programming and data science principles for epidemiology and health policy research.

These materials were adapted from materials from the 2024-2025 offerings of EPI/CHPR 202 at Stanford University, and were authored by [Anna Nguyen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/annatnguyen98/) and [Samuel Jaros](https://www.linkedin.com/in/samuel-jaros/). Anna Nguyen converted course materials into this online course with the assistance of [Cursor](https://cursor.com/)

You do not need R installed on your computer to use this site. The tutorials and homework pages include interactive code cells powered by [WebR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/) and [Quarto](https://quarto.org). If you prefer working locally, see the [Install R and RStudio](appendix/install_r_rstudio.qmd) appendix for setup instructions.

## Running R in your browser with WebR

[WebR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/) is a version of R compiled to run entirely in your web browser. Every interactive code cell on this site is an editable text window—click inside it, change the code, and run it when you are ready.

**To run code:**

- Click **Run Code** to execute everything in the cell. Printed output, tables, and plots appear directly below the cell.
- Press **Shift + Enter** as a keyboard shortcut for **Run Code**.
- Select part of the code and press **Ctrl + Enter** (Windows/Linux) or **Cmd + Enter** (Mac) to run just the selection—or run the current line if nothing is selected.

**Other controls:**

- Click the reset icon (↻) to restore the cell's original code and start over.
- Click the copy icon to copy the code to your clipboard.

The first time you run code on a page, WebR needs to download R and any required packages. This can take 30–60 seconds on a slow connection. Subsequent cells on the same page run much faster.

Try it below—edit the message if you like, then click **Run Code**:

```{webr-r}
print("Hello world!")
```

## How to use this site

- **Tutorials** — Interactive lessons that walk through R concepts week by week. Work through the code cells as you read.
- **Homework** — Practice assignments with editable code cells. Complete them in your browser, or download the source files from the [course GitHub repo](https://github.com/r-pophealth-research/online-course) to work in RStudio.
